# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- The routes, by name. Speech reaches Mute and Blind, and never Deaf. Gestures
  reach Deaf and Mute, and never Blind. Deaf can speak and gesture, Mute can
  only gesture, Blind can only speak. Check every message against this list
  before you send it.

- Deaf invents the gesture code out loud before anything else moves, and
  everyone else's opening move is waiting for it. The manual's verdict reaches
  Blind only as Deaf's spoken order.

- Whatever the code becomes, it starts by being able to say YES, NO, HOLD and
  DONE. Grow it only when a message will not fit.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I will establish the minimum shared gesture vocabulary before any bomb action: thumbs up means YES, thumbs down means NO, raised palm means HOLD, and the OK sign means DONE. I will not add more symbols until a message requires them. Both teammates should wait after receiving this code.

``` 
speak(text="Gesture code: thumbs up means YES. Thumbs down means NO. Raised palm means HOLD. The OK sign means DONE. Use only these four gestures for now. Mute and Blind, wait for further instructions.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The visible bomb state is unchanged, and I have received no new signal. I need the Mute monkey to inspect the manual and report its verdict to me using the agreed gesture code; I can then convert that verdict into spoken instructions for the Blind monkey.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Read the manual now. Report its verdict to me with the agreed gestures: thumbs up YES, thumbs down NO, raised palm HOLD, OK DONE. If the verdict needs information beyond this code, signal HOLD and we will extend the code.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

Mute has signaled HOLD, so the manual does not authorize an action yet. I am telling Blind to keep the bomb in its current state and wait; no wire should be touched or changed.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="The manual's current verdict is HOLD. Do not touch or change anything. Keep the bomb in its current state and wait.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The bomb remains unchanged. Mute’s HOLD gesture was relayed to Blind as a command not to touch anything, but it is ambiguous whether HOLD is the manual’s actual verdict or merely a request for a larger code. I will ask Mute to resolve that using the existing vocabulary.

``` 
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🖖"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

Mute has again sent the agreed HOLD gesture. I therefore treat the manual’s current instruction as HOLD, not as a request to decode a new symbol. The bomb remains stable, so Blind must not cut or manipulate any wire. I will also tell Mute that the verdict has been relayed.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Mute reports the manual verdict: HOLD. Do not touch the bomb or alter any wire. Wait.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The bomb still shows display 8 with a green light and red, yellow, and blue wires, with no new input from Mute. I will provide the complete visible state to both teammates and reiterate that Blind must not act while the manual’s verdict is HOLD.

``` 
speak(text="Current bomb state: display 8, green light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. The manual verdict remains HOLD. Blind, do not touch or alter anything.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

Mute has again signaled HOLD, but that does not distinguish an explicit manual instruction to hold from a request for more communication capacity. I will ask a precise yes/no question using the existing code: thumbs up means the manual explicitly says to hold; thumbs down means it does not. Blind must continue waiting until this is resolved.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Question: does the manual explicitly instruct us to HOLD the bomb unchanged right now? Signal thumbs up for YES or thumbs down for NO. Signal raised palm only if you cannot answer with those.")
speak(to="blind", text="The manual instruction is not yet disambiguated. Do not touch the bomb or wires; wait.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Mute answered NO: the manual does not explicitly say to hold the bomb unchanged. Since no safe action has been identified, Blind must still wait. I will test the first possible wire instruction directly; Mute can answer with the established YES/NO gestures.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Does the manual instruct Blind to cut wire 1, the red wire? Signal thumbs up for YES or thumbs down for NO.")
speak(to="blind", text="The manual does not say to HOLD, but no action is yet confirmed. Do not touch any wire; wait for the manual's specific instruction.")
wait()
```
